text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Iraq has bought an additional 100,000 tonnes of French wheat, lifting its total purchases of French wheat under the United Nations oil-for-food agreement to 300,000 tonnes, European grain traders said. The French wheat for January-February delivery was priced at $200 a tonne C and F for delivery to Jordan's port of Aqaba, they said. Additional costs linked to the transport by truck of the grain to Baghdad put the purchase at $230 a tonne, delivery Baghdad.

WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan issued separate tenders for 270,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better soft white wheat and Australian white milling wheat for Jan 8-31. Offers are to be opened at 1100 Pakistan Standard Time December 22 and remain valid until 1800 PST December 23. U.S. grain would be under GSM 102. On the same date, it seeks 270,000 tonnes of Australian white milling wheat.
- Sri Lanka may seek in early January 100,000 tonnes optional origin wheat for late January shipment, U.S. exporters said.
CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - Malaysia's Soon Soon Sdn Bhd passed on a tender for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and soybeans after finding the price too high, traders said on Friday.

SOYBEAN OIL TENDER - The CCC of the USDA said it will tender for 10,370 tonnes of U.S. bulk crude degummed soybean oil for donation to Peru. The delivery period was slated for February 3-18. Offers were requested by January 7. Successful offerers will be notified on January 8.
RICE TENDER - The Japanese Food Agency will hold an import tender for 7,000 tonnes of rice on December 25, agency officials said on Friday.
MARKET TALK - Tunisia may seek 100,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat as early as next week for delivery in January and February, several U.S. exporters said.

... A European Union trade committee rejected a proposal to open a 30,000-tonne reduced tariff quota for imports of U.S. malting barley, a European Commission spokesman said. On December 4 the Commission proposed the quota, which would have been valid for the rest of 1996 and would have allowed the import of U.S. malting barley at 50 percent of the full duty.

... Further wheat purchases may be expected from Iraq, which went on a buying spree this week to celebrate its return to world grain markets, European grain traders said. Iraq covered nearly half its import needs for the next six months on Thursday, buying 300,000 tonnes of wheat from France and 250,000 from Australia.
